vertices.note: Independent check. The historic Rue des Trois Renards enters the west side of Rue du Taur below Place Saint-Sernin. Matched road centre junction to shared OSM node 60960446, not the nearby shape node 6871954702. Historical scan inspected at original pixels; modern named-way connections inspected in the 2026-10-06 OSM snapshot. Estimated manual uncertainty 4–6 m; pedestrian junction geometry has changed.

Historic Rue Perigord opens on the east side of Rue du Taur; shared node belongs to both modern named ways. Original-pixel road-centre intersection inspected in the scan and modern OSM geometry. Estimated manual uncertainty 3–5 m. Supersedes imported fit jourdan-046 without deleting it.

Historic Rue de l Esquile approaches Rue du Taur obliquely from the southwest, just south of Perigord. Matched the centre of this distinctive junction to shared OSM node 60965710. Both the original scan and modern named-way geometry were inspected. Estimated manual uncertainty 4–6 m; this is a junction match, not interpolation along the modern line.
2026-10-06 review: DO NOT FIT yet. The historic oblique/wide mouth is ambiguous and the initial fit worsened held-out Montoyol and other pilot checks. The provisional correspondence is retained for human review; it is excluded from exported GCPs.

Independent check. Rue Montoyol enters Rue du Taur from the east, immediately south of the Esquile junction. Matched the road-centre junction to shared OSM node 60960444; not used in the fit. Original scan and modern named-way geometry inspected. Closely spaced junctions and old street width imply 4–6 m manual uncertainty.

Independent check. Historic Rue du Senechal enters Rue du Taur from the east north of Notre-Dame du Taur. Matched the centre of the street mouth to shared OSM node 60960443. Original scan and modern named-way geometry inspected. Estimated manual uncertainty 4–6 m; not used in fitting.

South end of Rue du Taur at the northern edge of Place du Capitole, where the historic Louis-Napoleon/Lafayette alignment enters from the east. Modern short section is named Rue Dominique Baudis. OSM node 60960442 links Taur, Baudis and Capitole. Matched the road-centre opening, not a square corner. Estimated uncertainty 5–8 m due to pedestrianisation and widened mouths; compare carefully. Supersedes imported fit jourdan-038 without deleting it.
